summary: Discovery / scoping call to define success criteria for a 6-week POC: prioritize open-model shortlist for medical summarization and multilingual notes extraction, size workload (qps / seq length), define benchmarks (accuracy/hallucination/latency), and agree next steps.
topics: Model quality tradeoffs: medical hallucination vs latency
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-28 16:00 UTC | Duration: 56m
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (GamaHeal Head of ML), Rajesh (CTO), Laura (Compliance), Ben (Platform), Alex (Product)

00:00 Sofia: ok everyone thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood inference, uh Ethan and Priya are with me from the solutions team. um Maya, Rajesh, Laura, great to have you. Can you do a quick round robin?
00:12 Maya: sure, Maya, Head of ML at GamaHeal, we run clinical summarization for remote consults, lots of multi-lingual notes, want to reduce manual QA.
00:22 Rajesh: Rajesh, CTO, focused on scale and infra compatibility, we prefer VPC/private control plane for PHI.
00:30 Laura: Laura, compliance, SOC2 in progress, will need KMS + audit logs details.
00:38 Ben: Ben, platform, will own integration and underlying k8s infra.
00:44 Alex: Alex, product, care about latency and UX for clinicians.
00:50 Ethan: cool thanks. high-level goal for this POC?
00:55 Maya: we want a model shortlist that balances factuality on medical notes, low hallucination, good multi-lingual support (EN, ES, PT), and that can run in our privacy constraints. also cost matters.
01:10 Priya: great, will focus on open-models but we can include verified hosted variants; our typical candidates are Lama2 70b (we heard), Falcon-180b, Mistral, Mosaic's open chat, and some quantized med-specialized variants.
01:28 Rajesh: quick note: we need 95th pctl latency under 350ms for single-turn summaries, batch background jobs can be slower. Also concurrency: baseline 50 qps, burst to 200 qps for peak clinic times.
01:43 Sofia: got it. on sequence lengths what are we seeing?
01:47 Ben: average consult notes are 600-900 tokens, with long threads up to 3k tokens occasionally. so we care about 2k-3k context support.
01:57 Maya: yes and multilingual tokenization differences matter because Spanish notes are denser.
02:04 Ethan: ok important because some open models degrade on long contexts and hallucinate. for this POC we should test at 512, 2k, and 3k seq lengths.
02:16 Sofia: success criteria — what are must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
02:20 Maya: must: accuracy on key entities (medication, dosage, diagnosis) with F1 > 0.88; hallucination rate < 5% on a curated set; privacy: model run inside VPC or equivalent (no vendor data copy). nice-to-have: sub-300ms 95th pctl latency, cost under $X per 1k summaries (we'll share target).
02:40 Laura: compliance must include KMS integration for key material, audit logs for inference requests and RBAC. we will need SOC2 artifacts.
02:51 Ethan: commercially, Redwood can do Dedicated or Private modes; Dedicated gives reserved capacity and SLA; Private gives customer-managed control plane. for PHI you likely want Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.
03:06 Rajesh: leaning Private but want rollout plan. we must see benchmarks first.
03:12 Priya: suggested POC structure: Week 0-1: data ingest + de-id + baseline runs on small subset; Week 2: bulk benchmarking across three seq lengths and multilingual samples; Week 3: latency/throughput tuning (batching, KV cache, quantization); Week 4: integration of outputs into our QA pipeline; Week 5: clinical review of outputs; Week 6: decision and next steps.
03:40 Alex: sounds reasonable. what models do you suggest we shortlist for the med domain?
03:45 Ethan: for open models we recommend: Llama-2-70b (if you quantize), Falcon-180B-Instruct, Mistral-Instruct / Mixtral variants, and MosaicML's MPT-30B derivatives; we also have Redwood-verified quantized variants (labelled in our catalog). We can include med-specialized checkpoints if you want to test factuality.
04:05 Maya: question — which of these tend to hallucinate less on meds and dosages?
04:10 Priya: in our benching we've seen tapestry: some instruction-tuned Mistral and fine-tuned smaller models actually make fewer dosage errors because they are calibrated; larger Llama variants are fluent but can hallucinate numbers unless prompt templates + verification checks are used.
04:28 Ben: how about hallucination measurement — how do you measure?
04:31 Ethan: we'll use a combination: automated entity matching (F1), a hallucination classifier on golden triples, and clinical raters for a sampled set. quantify as percent of statements with unsupported facts.
04:45 Sofia: workload sizing — you said 50 qps baseline, burst 200; memory constraints?
04:50 Ben: available GPUs are A10/A100 equivalent in our private cluster, but cost is a concern. we prefer 16-24GB per device if possible.
04:59 Priya: that maps to 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants; Redwood can suggest quant profiles that preserve quality while reducing memory.
05:08 Rajesh: timeline for bench results?
05:11 Ethan: if you provide de-id data by Mar 4, Redwood can run baseline bench and return a short report by Mar 10 (week 2). tuning and a deeper perf pass by Mar 17.
05:22 Maya: are there examples of similar customers? any benchmarks for multilingual medical notes?
05:26 Sofia: we can share anonymized benchmark snippets and a previous med-POC summary, will redact company names.
05:32 Laura: security docs — we need encryption at rest, KMS integration details and proof of log retention policies.
05:38 Sofia: sure we'll send SOC2 + security pack and a short runbook for Private deployment options.
05:44 Alex: what's the pilot acceptance criteria again?
05:47 Maya: 0) entity F1 > 0.88; 1) hallucination < 5%; 2) reviewers rate summaries >= 4/5 for clinical usefulness on sampled notes; 3) deployment must meet our VPC + KMS constraints.
06:05 Ethan: ok we'll bake those into the benchmark template.
06:08 Priya: quick tradeoffs note — you can often reduce hallucination by adding verifier stage (small model check or retrieval augmented step) but that adds latency and cost. we'll include a recommended fallback: use a lightweight verifier for dosage fields only.
06:24 Ben: could we do a hybrid routing: hosted for non-PHI (faster) and private for PHI?
06:29 Rajesh: maybe, but that increases complexity and audit surface. we likely keep everything in Private for now.
06:36 Sofia: action items recap: we'll send pricing + benchmark template; Redwood to propose model shortlist with recommended instance types; GamaHeal to provide de-id dataset; compliance to confirm SOC2 scoping contact.
06:52 Maya: ok schedule SE deep dive next week to dig into KV cache behavior and batching details.
06:58 Sofia: sounds good, thanks all. end of call.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcribed product names (Lama2/Llama2 variations) and filler words; timestamps approximate.
notes: Customer strongly prefers Private deployment due to PHI. Multilingual support (EN/ES/PT) is a hard requirement. POC to emphasize hallucination metrics and entity-level F1 for meds/dosage.
benchmarks_agreed: Measure: Entity F1 for meds/dosage, hallucination percent (automated + human sample), ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summary overlap, latency (p50/p95), throughput at 50qps baseline and 200qps burst; test seq lengths 512/2048/3072; languages EN/ES/PT.
timeline_agreed: 6-week POC: data ingest (week0-1), bench (week2), tuning (week3), integration (week4), clinical review (week5), decision (week6)
